properties.trigger: any competition in softball; a softball game, doubleheader, lineup, box score, rainout, forfeit, standings or tournament; a softball position, stat or stage not yet in this world
properties.scope: competition, season, team, person, event, venue, stat_line

data.short_description: Vocabulary for recreational slow-pitch softball (with fast-pitch notes): positions, stages, decided_by values, batting/pitching/fielding stat keys, standings and tiebreakers, co-ed lineup rules, subs and ringers, forfeits, rainouts and makeups.

lore.title: Overview
lore.content:
Sport code: softball. This pack is written for recreational slow-pitch softball: parks-and-rec, company, church and bar leagues, co-ed or single-gender, adults. It also covers rec fast-pitch with the notes at the end of this chunk. competition.match_format is slowpitch (the default) or fastpitch; an event's match_format overrides it for a one-off game in the other form. Baseball is a separate pack (code baseball). Shared keys are spelled identically in the baseball and softball packs: decided_by run_rule, called_game and time_limit; stat keys outs_pitched and games_booked; and the exhibition tag on match lines that must not sum into a season.
A match is a game. A game is seven innings, each with a top (away bats) and a bottom (home bats); the home team is the one in the bottom half and usually comes from the league schedule, not from whose field it is, since every game is at the park complex. Most games are also under a time limit (commonly 55-70 minutes, no new inning after time) and a run rule (commonly 20 after 3, 15 after 4, 10 after 5; the league's exact line goes in House rules). Games are often played as doubleheaders: two games, same night, same two teams or two different opponents. Record each game as its own match event with round Game 1 and Game 2.
The single score number is runs: home_score and away_score. score_display carries anything the numbers lose: innings when not seven ("17-2 (5 inn.)"), how it ended ("9-9 (time)"), the state when rain stopped it ("5-3 Rovers, top 3rd, rain"). Seven innings is the sport's default, so regulation_length is set only when a game is scheduled for a different length ("5" for a short-format or youth game, "9" for a league that plays nine). A line score, when the owner keeps one, is optional and lives in event.periods: one object per inning with number, home and away (home null for a bottom half not played).
Ties exist and are normal. A game that ends level when time expires is result tie, not draw, and both COMPETED_IN edges get result tie. Some leagues play one extra inning or an international tiebreaker (runner on second to start the inning); see Stages and rounds for decided_by.
Default competition: level recreational, format league_playoffs (a round robin of 8-14 games then a single-elimination end-of-season tournament) or round_robin when there is no tournament, scoring_system win_loss. Standings run on W-L-T with ties counting a half win, unless House rules say the league uses points (2-1-0).
A person can play in two leagues at once (Tuesday rec league, Thursday company league): one person, one PLAYS_FOR edge per team, both competitions under this pack, and stat lines carry for_team. Season names include the competition so lines never collide.
Fast-pitch note: everything here applies with these differences, which a fast-pitch competition records in its House rules chunk: pitching matters (use the full pitching key group and the extended pitching keys), stolen bases and bunts are live, there is no extra-hitter-by-default and no co-ed alternation, the arc rule does not exist, and the run rule is usually 8 after 5 or 10 after 5. Set the competition's match_format to fastpitch so the AI knows to ask for pitching lines.
Every entity in this sport carries the tag softball. Matches carry the season tag (e.g. riverside-coed-spring-2026) and match.

lore.title: Positions
lore.content:
Position codes for PLAYS_FOR position and secondary_positions, and for PLAYED_IN position on the day. Slow-pitch plays ten in the field (four outfielders); fast-pitch plays nine.
P: pitcher
C: catcher
1B: first base
2B: second base
3B: third base
SS: shortstop
LF: left field
LCF: left-centre field (slow-pitch, four-outfielder alignment)
RCF: right-centre field (slow-pitch, four-outfielder alignment)
CF: centre field (fast-pitch or three-outfielder leagues)
RF: right field
EH: extra hitter, bats but does not field (some leagues call it EP, extra player; use EH)
DH: designated hitter (fast-pitch only; bats for the pitcher)
FLEX: fast-pitch only, the fielder the DH bats for
UT: utility, plays anywhere; use as a roster position for the person who really does
ROV: rover or short fielder, a fifth infielder in leagues that play one instead of a fourth outfielder
On the roster edge, position is where the person usually plays. A person who plays everywhere gets UT with secondary_positions listing the real spots. Nobody is recorded as "bench": a rec roster has no bench, only who showed up, and that is a PLAYED_IN edge with played true or false.
Roles on PLAYS_FOR: starter means a regular, rotation means plays when numbers are short, captain is the one who talks to the umpire, captain_organiser is not a PLAYS_FOR role (use STAFF_OF role captain_organiser alongside the player edge). Do not use practice_squad or taxi here.

lore.title: Stages and rounds
lore.content:
Season stage values (season.stage and event.stage):
preseason: a practice game or scrimmage before the schedule starts; stat lines from these are tagged exhibition and never roll into season totals.
regular_season: the scheduled round robin. round is "Week N" and, on a doubleheader night, the event's round is "Week N Game 1" / "Week N Game 2".
playoff: the end-of-season tournament. round is one of: Play-in, Round of 16, Quarterfinal, Semifinal, Final, Third place, and for double elimination add the bracket: "Winners Semifinal", "Losers Final", "Grand Final", "If necessary".
consolation: a consolation bracket for teams knocked out early, when the league runs one.
exhibition: all-star game, a friendly against another league, a charity game; stat lines tagged exhibition.
A tournament weekend is a parent event (event_type match, stage playoff, name "<Season> Tournament", date_* of day one and end_date of the last day, score_display left blank) with each game PART_OF it as well as PART_OF the season. A rained-out game that never started keeps its event and its round and moves its date; a game abandoned after play began and replayed from scratch is a new event with round "Replay" (see Forfeits and abandonments).
decided_by values (set only when the game did not run its full seven innings to a natural end, or went past them):
regulation: seven innings, natural end. Default; may be left blank.
run_rule: ended early because one side led by the league's run-rule margin at the end of an inning. Use this spelling, which the baseball pack shares, so a season is not split across two spellings.
time_limit: the time limit ended the game (whether ahead, behind or tied). A game that ends in a tie on time is result tie, decided_by time_limit.
extra_innings: went past seven innings and was settled in the extra inning(s).
international_tiebreaker: extra inning(s) started with a runner on second, as the league rule provides.
called_game: an umpire called the game before its natural end for weather, darkness or field conditions, after it had become official (the league's official-game line, commonly four complete innings or three and a half with the home side ahead). status stays completed.
forfeit: the result was awarded without a full game being played; status forfeited.
A game that was stopped before it was official is status abandoned, result no_result, decided_by blank.

lore.title: Stat keys
lore.content:
All keys lowercase snake_case, values numbers, null for not recorded. Rec books are partial most weeks: store what was kept, leave the rest null, never write zero for "nobody counted". A derived number is only computed over lines where every component it needs is non-null, and the answer says how many games that covers. Every stat_line carries completeness: full when every key this chunk lists for its scope was recorded, partial when any key is null because nobody kept it, unknown for a typed-in total of unknown coverage; sums skip nulls and a season line built from any partial line is partial.
PLAYER BATTING (match, season, career, split lines)
plate_appearances: times at the plate with a result (stored; when unknown derive as at_bats + walks + hit_by_pitch + sacrifice_flies + sacrifice_bunts over non-null components)
at_bats: official at bats, excluding walks, sacrifices and hit-by-pitch (stored)
runs: runs scored (stored)
hits: all hits (stored)
singles: derived as hits - doubles - triples - home_runs when the extra-base keys are non-null; store it only if the owner counts it directly
doubles: two-base hits (stored)
triples: three-base hits (stored)
home_runs: home runs, over the fence or inside the park (stored)
rbi: runs batted in (stored)
walks: bases on balls, including intentional (stored)
intentional_walks: intentional walks, when the league counts them (stored)
strikeouts: struck out, including looking at a third strike in slow-pitch (stored)
hit_by_pitch: hit by pitch; rare in slow-pitch, live in fast-pitch (stored)
sacrifice_flies: sac flies (stored)
sacrifice_bunts: sac bunts; fast-pitch mostly (stored)
stolen_bases: fast-pitch or leagues that allow stealing (stored)
caught_stealing: fast-pitch (stored)
grounded_into_double_play: GIDP (stored)
reached_on_error: times the batter reached on a fielding error (stored; counts as an at bat, not a hit)
total_bases: derived as singles + 2*doubles + 3*triples + 4*home_runs
batting_average: derived, hits / at_bats; quote with the number of games and at bats it covers; league qualifying minimum is House rules (default 2 plate appearances per team game played)
on_base_percentage: derived, (hits + walks + hit_by_pitch) / (at_bats + walks + hit_by_pitch + sacrifice_flies); when a component is null on every line say the OBP is approximate and name the missing part
slugging_percentage: derived, total_bases / at_bats
ops: derived, on_base_percentage + slugging_percentage
home_run_count_remaining: see Extended keys for leagues with a per-game home-run cap; not a default key
PLAYER PITCHING (slow-pitch: usually just who pitched and how many walks; fast-pitch: the full group)
games_pitched: appearances on the mound (stored)
games_started_pitching: starts (stored)
outs_pitched: outs recorded while pitching (stored; the honest unit, since thirds of an inning do not add)
innings_pitched: derived, outs_pitched / 3, written as 6.2 for 20 outs
hits_allowed: hits allowed (stored)
runs_allowed: runs allowed, earned or not (stored)
earned_runs: earned runs, only when the book separates them (stored)
walks_allowed: walks issued (stored)
strikeouts_pitching: batters struck out (stored)
home_runs_allowed: home runs allowed (stored)
wins_pitching, losses_pitching: pitcher decisions, only in leagues that credit them (stored)
earned_run_average: derived, earned_runs * 7 / innings_pitched (seven-inning game; use 9 only if House rules say so)
walks_per_game: derived, walks_allowed * 7 / innings_pitched
PLAYER FIELDING
putouts: putouts (stored)
assists: assists (stored)
errors: fielding errors (stored)
double_plays_turned: double plays taken part in (stored)
passed_balls: catcher (stored)
fielding_percentage: derived, (putouts + assists) / (putouts + assists + errors)
innings_fielded: derived from PLAYED_IN when the owner tracks substitutions; otherwise do not compute
PLAYER PARTICIPATION
games_played: on season and career lines this is the stat_line property, not a stats key: the number of match lines summed. A season line typed in by the owner sets games_played to what they say.
TEAM MATCH LINE (one per team per game; runs stay on the event and are never repeated here)
hits, doubles, triples, home_runs, walks, strikeouts, errors, left_on_base, double_plays_turned, stolen_bases: team totals, same meanings as above (stored)
Runs by inning are not stat keys; a line score belongs in event.periods (number, home, away per inning), optional.
TEAM SEASON LINE: see Standings.

lore.title: Standings
lore.content:
Team season line keys (scope season, subject_kind team, RECORDED_IN the season, STAT_OF the team), all stored and rebuilt from COMPETED_IN results and match scores:
wins: games won, including forfeit wins
losses: games lost, including forfeit losses
ties: games tied
forfeit_wins: of the wins, how many were awarded by forfeit
forfeit_losses: of the losses, how many were forfeits
no_results: games abandoned with no result (not counted in games_played)
runs_for: runs scored across completed and forfeited games (forfeits count at the awarded score, default 7-0, unless House rules exclude them)
runs_against: runs allowed, same basis
games_booked: how many of the team's completed games have at least one player match line, so the AI can say "8 of 12 games have a book" before quoting averages
points: only when the league runs a points table (House rules, e.g. 2-1-0); otherwise leave null
Derived, never stored: games_played = wins + losses + ties (also set the stat_line property games_played to this); win_pct = (wins + 0.5 * ties) / games_played; run_differential = runs_for - runs_against; games_back from the leader when asked.
Columns to show: Team, W, L, T, Pct, RF, RA, Diff, and Streak when asked. Add Pts when the league uses points. Group by division (COMPETES_IN group) when the league has them.
Tiebreakers, in this order, unless the competition's House rules chunk lists its own (most parks departments publish one; ask once and store it):
1. win_pct
2. head-to-head record among the tied teams
3. run_differential, with a per-game cap of 10 if House rules say so (many leagues cap differential per game to blunt run-ups; note the cap when applied)
4. runs_against (fewer is better)
5. runs_for
6. coin flip or league decision, recorded in lore on the season titled Tiebreak
Forfeits: a forfeit counts as a win or loss in the record. Several leagues drop a team after two or three forfeits; that is a COMPETES_IN status withdrawn, outcome withdrew, and remaining games against them are status cancelled with a lore note, or forfeited in favour of the opponent, as the league rules.
Playoff seeding comes from this table; write each team's seed on COMPETES_IN seed when the bracket is set.

lore.title: Roster rules
lore.content:
Roster: rec rosters run 12-20 players; most leagues require a minimum on the league roster (often 10-11) and a minimum to start a game (commonly 8, with 9 or 10 in some leagues; a short side plays with an automatic out in the empty lineup slot in some rules, fields short in others). Store the league's numbers in House rules on the competition. A team below the minimum at game time forfeits; see Forfeits and abandonments.
Fielders: slow-pitch plays 10 in the field, co-ed leagues usually five and five; fast-pitch plays 9. Batting order may be longer than the fielders: one or two extra hitters (EH) in most leagues, and some co-ed leagues let everyone who shows up bat. Before logging a lineup, check what you can check: no more fielders than the league allows, no two people at the same fielding position, EH count within the league's limit, minimum players met. Say what you checked in one line.
Co-ed alternation: co-ed leagues usually require the batting order to alternate men and women and often cap the number of men in the field. This world does not record anyone's gender, so you cannot check alternation and should not try to infer it from names. Say once, lightly: "I've checked the count and positions; you'll want to eyeball the alternation yourself." Never add a gender key, tag or position code to do this check.
Substitutes and ringers: a fill-in from outside the roster who plays one night gets a PLAYS_FOR edge with arrangement substitute, started and ended on the game date, acquired_via unknown, and a lore note on the event titled Subs saying who filled in for whom. A sub who keeps coming back gets a normal open edge with arrangement amateur from their first game; close the one-night edges and say so. A person who plays for two teams in two leagues simply has two open edges, and their match lines carry for_team.
Availability: when someone is out, set availability unavailable (or doubtful) on their PLAYS_FOR edge and nothing else. Do not ask why. If the owner gives a reason that is about a body (sliding into second, a hamstring, surgery, pregnancy, a doctor), leave it out and say once: "I don't keep anything about injuries on file, but I've got Mike down as out." Clear availability when they are back. If the owner wants to remember who was missing on a night, PLAYED_IN with played false does it without a word about why.
Minors: a 16- or 17-year-old on a waiver is is_minor true, first name and last initial, position and team, nothing else, and no web search ever. Kids in the dugout, kids keeping the book, family on the bleachers: not recorded at all.
Organiser, treasurer, scorekeeper: STAFF_OF edges to the team with role captain_organiser (plus their PLAYS_FOR edge), treasurer, or other with title Scorekeeper. Dues: this pack does not track money as data. If the owner wants a reminder of who has paid, keep it as one lore chunk on the team titled "Dues <season label>" in the owner's words, no amounts on people, no payment details, and do not compute balances.
Jersey numbers are rarely meaningful; store them if given.

lore.title: Officials
lore.content:
OFFICIATED role values:
plate_umpire: the umpire behind the plate; most rec games have only this one
base_umpire: a second umpire in the field, when the league pays for two
scorer: an official or league scorekeeper, when the league keeps its own book
field_supervisor: the parks department or league rep on site who makes rainout and forfeit calls
Umpires in rec leagues are private people working for a few dollars a game: record a name only when the owner gives it, never look one up, and keep complaints about calls in event lore titled Key moments in the owner's words.

lore.title: Extended keys
lore.content:
No extended keys yet. Add keys here, one per line with a plain meaning and the date added, before using them in a stat line.
Likely candidates, not active until added: home_runs_over_cap (home runs that counted as outs under a per-game home-run limit), courtesy_runner_appearances, walk_off_hits, games_umpired (for a player who also umpires), beer_league_awards (do not; use WON edges with a title instead).

lore.title: Forfeits and abandonments
lore.content:
Forfeit: status forfeited, decided_by forfeit, awarded score in home_score/away_score (default 7-0 to the team that showed up; House rules may say 1-0 or "W/L only"), result from the event's point of view, COMPETED_IN result win/loss, and why in a lore chunk titled Forfeit in the owner's words (short-handed, no-show, ineligible player, ejection). A forfeit counts in the standings line, including forfeit_wins / forfeit_losses, and in runs_for/runs_against at the awarded score unless House rules exclude it.
Forfeit then a friendly: teams often play anyway once the forfeit is recorded. Any stat lines from that game are tagged exhibition and never summed into season lines; mention it in the Forfeit chunk.
Rainout before the first pitch: status postponed, keep the event, update the date when the league reschedules, original date in lore titled Reschedule. Never create a second event. If the league never makes it up, status cancelled.
Rain or darkness after play began but before the game was official: status abandoned, result no_result, score and inning in score_display, nothing in decided_by; COMPETED_IN result no_result on both edges. If the league replays it from scratch, the abandoned event stays on the books and the replay is a new event with round "Replay"; player match lines from the abandoned game are tagged exhibition unless House rules say partial games count. If the league resumes from the point of stoppage, it is a suspended game, not an abandoned one: keep the one event, status suspended, date_* stay the first night, end_date the night it finished, both dates in score_display while it waits ("5-3, susp. top 3rd, resumes 2026-06-17"), stat lines accumulate on it, status completed when it finishes, and the result counts in the standings on the completion date.
Called after official: status completed, decided_by called_game, score_display with innings and cause ("8-6 (4.5 inn., rain)"). Counts fully.
Run rule: status completed, decided_by run_rule, innings in score_display.
Time limit: status completed, decided_by time_limit; tied means result tie.
Doubleheader with one game lost to weather: two events, each with its own status; do not merge them.
Whole-night rainout at the complex: every event that night is postponed; say how many you moved.
Dropped team: COMPETES_IN status withdrawn, outcome withdrew, and each remaining game against them handled per the league (forfeit to the opponent or cancelled). Standings note how many games each team has left as a result.

lore.title: Glossary
lore.content:
Arc rule: the pitched ball must arc between the league's limits (commonly 6-12 feet); an illegal pitch is a ball unless swung at. Not recorded.
Book: the scorebook. "Was the book kept?" is the first question before quoting any average.
Bomb, dinger, tater: home run. Jack: also home run. Over the fence vs inside the park: both home_runs; the difference goes in lore if anyone cares.
Courtesy runner: a runner substituted for a batter who reached base, allowed by many leagues; the batter's stats are unaffected, the runner's run counts for the runner. Only track if the owner does.
EH / EP: extra hitter / extra player; bats without fielding.
Flip-flop: when the away team is far ahead in the last inning, some leagues let the home team bat first in that inning to try to avoid a run rule. Note in lore; the score is the score.
Game 1 / Game 2: the two halves of a doubleheader.
Ghost runner: a slang name for the international tiebreaker runner on second.
Homer cap: a per-game limit on over-the-fence home runs; extras are outs. Extended key candidate.
Makeup: a rescheduled game. A postponed game keeps its event and moves its date; a replay of an abandoned game is a new event with round Replay.
Mercy / run rule: the same thing; always write decided_by run_rule.
Pitcher's screen: a protective net in front of the pitcher in some leagues; a ball hitting it is a dead ball. Not recorded.
Rainout line: the phone number or page where the parks department posts field closures; store the URL on the competition's website or a lore chunk titled Rainout line.
Ringer: a strong player brought in from outside the roster, see Roster rules.
Short-handed: fewer players than the lineup minimum; may mean an automatic out each time the empty slot comes up, or a forfeit, per House rules.
Spot, the: the bar after the game. A team's regular spot lives in a lore chunk on the team titled Traditions (or as a venue with venue_type other, tagged postgame-spot, no edge). What happened there goes in the event's lore titled Postgame, in the owner's words.
Walk-off: a game-ending hit by the home team. Lore, or Extended key walk_off_hits if the owner wants to count them.

lore.title: Season calendar
lore.content:
Spring (April-June), Summer (June-August) and Fall (September-October) leagues are common, each a separate season of the same competition (labels "Spring 2026", "Summer 2026", "Fall 2026"). Many teams play two seasons a year under one team entity; some change their name between seasons, in which case keep one team and note the name history in lore titled Names.
A typical season: 8-14 regular-season games over as many weeks (doubleheaders halve the weeks), one or two rainout weeks that push the schedule, then a single- or double-elimination tournament on the final weekend or over two weeknights. Set rounds_total to the scheduled regular-season games per team. Set stage to playoff once the bracket starts and current_round as the bracket moves.
Registration and the organiser meeting are events with event_type meeting, PART_OF the season, when the owner wants them on the timeline. A tryout or a pickup night before the season is event_type tryout or practice, stage preseason.
When the season ends: final_rank and outcome on every COMPETES_IN edge, WON Champion (and Runner-up) to the season, an awards WON edge for anything the team gives out (team MVP, best glove, the sombrero), then offer to open the next season with the roster rolled over and arrangement substitute edges left closed.

properties.trigger: a softball game or doubleheader just happened; logging a softball score, lineup or box score; a softball batting average, OBP, slugging or leaderboard; what is coming up for the owner's softball team; who is available

data.short_description: The post-game log for a rec softball team in order: score the game(s), ask whether the book was kept, lineup and subs, player and team match lines with nulls for what nobody counted, roll up season lines, then the story. Also how to quote averages honestly from a sporadic book.

lore.title: What this covers
lore.content: The thirty-second log after a rec softball night, and the honest question before any average: was the book kept? This workflow owns the tags book-kept, no-book and exhibition on match events and stat lines in softball. It runs on top of rule/recording_a_match and rule/stats and only adds the softball order of operations.

lore.title: Logging a night
lore.content:
1. Find the night. search_entities entity_type event, the season tag, the date. A scheduled event usually exists (the schedule was loaded at onboarding); update it rather than creating. A doubleheader is two events, round "Week N Game 1" and "Week N Game 2".
2. Score each game first, before anything else: status, home_score, away_score, score_display when innings or ending need saying, periods if the owner read out a line score, result, decided_by (run_rule, time_limit, extra_innings, international_tiebreaker, called_game, forfeit), COMPETED_IN result on both edges. Confirm which side was home for the night if the owner's wording ("we won 12-4") leaves it open; the schedule usually says.
3. Ask one question: "Did anyone keep the book?" If no: tag the event no-book and stop at the score and a Summary lore chunk. If yes or partly: tag the event book-kept and take the lines.
4. Lineup, if the competition is lineups-tracked: PLAYED_IN per player with for_team, lineup_order, position, started. Check fielder count, duplicate positions, EH count and the minimum, and say what you checked. Subs: a one-night PLAYS_FOR edge (arrangement substitute) and a Subs lore chunk.
5. Player match lines: one stat_line per player per game, scope match, subject_kind player, RECORDED_IN the event, STAT_OF the person, for_team when the person has two open roster edges, keys from the pack, null for anything not kept, completeness partial when anything is null and full when the whole line was kept. Tag: softball, stats, the season tag, the player's slug fragment. Take the whole side in one batch; confirm first when it is more than eight new lines.
6. Team match line: hits, errors, left_on_base and the rest if kept; never runs.
7. Roll up: update each player's season line (derived, games_played = number of match lines, as_of the game date, Derived from chunk listing the match lines) and the team's season line (wins/losses/ties, forfeit counts, runs_for/against, games_booked). Do it in the same breath as the match lines; a stale season line is worse than none.
8. The story: Summary, Key moments, Postgame in the owner's words; umpire gripes stay in the owner's words too.
9. Say it back in two lines: the result and record, and what the book covered ("Book kept for 9 of 11 batters; Dana's RBI not recorded").

lore.title: Averages people will actually quote
lore.content:
Before quoting a batting average, OBP, slugging or a leaderboard: count the team's completed games (COMPETED_IN results that are win/loss/tie), count the games tagged book-kept, and lead with the coverage: "Over the 8 games with a book, Dana is 19-for-31, .613." A player's own coverage can be smaller than the team's (they missed games, or their line was not kept one night); use their match lines, not the team's count.
Qualifying minimum for a leaderboard: 2 plate appearances per team game booked, unless the competition's House rules set one. List the unqualified leaders under a "not enough at bats" line rather than hiding them.
Nulls: skip, never zero. A derived rate uses only the lines where every component is non-null and says how many games that is. If walks were never kept, OBP cannot be computed; say so and offer batting average instead.
Exhibition lines (tag exhibition: preseason, forfeit-then-friendly, all-star, replayed abandonments) are never summed into season or career lines. Mention them separately if asked.
If a typed-in season total (source owner) disagrees with your sum of match lines, show both and ask which to keep; do not overwrite.

lore.title: Game night reminders
lore.content:
When asked what is coming up: the next scheduled event(s) for the owner's team (tag mine), with field (HELD_AT field), start time, opponent, and whether it is a doubleheader. Add the rainout line (lore on the competition) when the forecast comes up in conversation; do not look up the weather unless asked and a weather tool exists.
Availability check before a game: list roster edges with availability unavailable or doubtful, by name only, no reasons, and the count of available players against the league minimum. Never ask why anyone is out.
